He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]]. LeVert was originally drafted by the [[Indiana Pacers]] but was traded to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] on draft night. He later played for the Pacers, [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], [[Atlanta Hawks]], and [[Detroit Pistons]]. ==Early life== LeVert grew up in [[Columbus, Ohio|Columbus]] but moved to [[Pickerington, Ohio]] in second grade. One of his teammates at [[Pickerington High School Central]] was future [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]] forward [[Jae'Sean Tate]].{{cite news |last1=Landis |first1=Bill |title=Ohio State basketball: How freshman Jae'Sean Tate became a vital part of Buckeyes' present and future |url=https://www.cleveland.com/osu/2015/03/ohio_state_basketball_jaesean_1.html |access-date=June 5, 2018 |work=[[The Plain-Dealer]] |date=March 11, 2015 |archive-date=August 28, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180828134447/https://www.cleveland.com/osu/2015/03/ohio_state_basketball_jaesean_1.html |url-status=live }} As a high school senior, he led Pickerington Central to a 26–2 record and the 2012 OHSAA Division I state championship. LeVert was a 2012 [[Associated Press]] All-Ohio Second Team high school basketball player and the 2012 ''[[Columbus Dispatch]]'' Metro Player of the Year for [[Pickerington High School Central]]. He was not heavily recruited in high school and his only official visit was to [[Alabama State Hornets basketball|Alabama State]].{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/bigten/2014/10/16/michigan-wolverines-caris-levert-nik-stauskas-trey-burke-guard/17387247/|title=Caris LeVert aims to be next Michigan guard to step up|access-date=October 21, 2014|date=October 16, 2014|author=Snyder, Mark|work=[[USA Today]]|archive-date=August 17, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170817042157/https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/bigten/2014/10/16/michigan-wolverines-caris-levert-nik-stauskas-trey-burke-guard/17387247/|url-status=live}} He committed to play basketball for [[John Groce]] and the [[Ohio Bobcats men's basketball]] program in November 2011. ===Freshman season=== [[File:20130323 Caris LeVert.jpg|thumb|left|LeVert defending against [[2012–13 VCU Rams men's basketball team|VCU]] in the [[2013 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2013 NCAA basketball tournament]]]] LeVert arrived at Michigan weighing {{convert|162|lbs|kg|1}}. As a freshman, he began the year behind Stauskas, Robinson, [[Tim Hardaway Jr.]], and Matt Vogrich on the [[depth chart]] for the [[shooting guard]]/[[small forward]] positions and did not play in the first six games as a result. LeVert was a part of an incoming class that included McGary, Stauskas, Robinson, and [[Spike Albrecht]].{{cite web|url=http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/02/28/assigned-reading-caris-leverts-defining-moment/|title=Assigned Reading: Caris LeVert's defining moment|access-date=March 14, 2014|date=February 28, 2014|publisher=[[NBC Sports]]|author=Payne, Terrence|archive-date=March 4, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140304180848/http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/02/28/assigned-reading-caris-leverts-defining-moment/|url-status=live}} Eventually, Michigan [[head coach]] [[John Beilein]] decided that LeVert had value as a perimeter defender and decided to play him rather than redshirt him.{{cite web|url=http://philadelphia.cbslocal.com/2014/01/07/rising-star-michigan-guard-caris-levert/|title=Rising Star: Michigan Guard Caris LeVert|access-date=March 13, 2014|date=January 7, 2014|publisher=[[KYW-TV]]|author=Kahn, Andrew|archive-date=July 2, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170702192512/http://philadelphia.cbslocal.com/2014/01/07/rising-star-michigan-guard-caris-levert/|url-status=live}} On December 1 against [[2012–13 Bradley Braves men's basketball team|Bradley]] Beilein juggled his lineup: Stauskas made his first career regular season start and LeVert saw his first action.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=323360071|title=(3) Michigan 74 (7-0, 1-0 away);
